deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is Riemann's handwritten draft of the opening sentence of his 1859 Berlin Academy paper 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse' (Monatsberichte der Königlich Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin, Nov. 1859). The draft reads approximately: 'Meinen Dank für die Auszeichnung, welche [gap left for a clause] glaube ich am besten dadurch zu erkennen zu geben, dass ich von der mir gütigst ertheilten Erlaubniß baldigst Gebrauch mache durch Mittheilung einer Untersuchung über die Häufigkeit der Primzahlen; ein Gegenstand, welcher durch das Interesse, welches Gauss und Dirichlet demselben längere Zeit geschenkt haben, einer solchen Mittheilung vielleicht nicht ganz unwerth erscheint.' In English: 'I believe I can best express my thanks for the distinction [...] by making early use of the permission kindly granted to me, through communicating an investigation of the frequency of prime numbers. This subject, through the interest that Gauss and Dirichlet showed in it over a long time, may perhaps not seem entirely unworthy of such a communication.' The published text fills the gap after 'welche' with 'mir die Akademie durch die Aufnahme unter ihre Correspondenten hat zu Theil werden lassen' and reads 'von der hierdurch erhaltenen Erlaubniss'. The draft therefore shows an earlier wording ('mir gütigst ertheilten'), with the clause about election as a Corresponding Member not yet written. Riemann was elected a corresponding member of the Berlin Academy in August 1859. The thanks and the 'permission' refer to a member's right to communicate papers to the Academy. The faint strokes on the rest of the sheet (plus signs, equals signs, fraction bars, symbols such as x^2) are show-through from writing on the other side, not content of this page. The next page continues the archival context: a note on the density of primes, a 'Nachtrag' with a revised ending for the paper, and draft letters (apparently to Kronecker and Borchardt) about Dirichlet's unpublished work on prime frequency and a Gauss–Encke letter.

results.what: Draft of the opening dedication/acknowledgment sentence of Riemann's 1859 prime-number paper, which names Gauss and Dirichlet as predecessors.
results.modern_name: Introductory paragraph of Riemann's 1859 memoir on the prime-counting function

deep.surprise_reason: This is a non-mathematical draft of the well-known first sentence of Riemann's 1859 paper. It differs only slightly in wording from the published text, and such drafts are known from the Nachlass.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 ends after 'welche' with a deliberate blank: the clause 'mir die Akademie durch die Aufnahme unter ihre Correspondenten hat zu Theil werden lassen' (as published) is not written here. It is not illegible text.
'Meinen[?] Dank für die Auszeichnung[?]' — both readings are consistent with the published text and can be accepted without question marks.
'am[?] besten' should read 'am besten' (as in the published text).

'mir gütigst[?] ertheilten Erlaubniß baldigst[?]' — this reading is plausible. The published version has 'hierdurch erhaltenen Erlaubniss', so this is a genuine draft variant, and 'baldigst' matches the published text.

The faint marks over the lower two-thirds of the sheet (crosses, equals signs, fraction strokes, isolated letters/exponents) are show-through from the reverse side. They should not be transcribed as content of folio 20v.
